doc.title: David Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 18, 2003

title: Staying with the church faith
summary: Murray kept his faith; anecdote of a quartet colleague running out during an earthquake crying for Jesus.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Did you retain the faith part of the church?

Uh yes, I did. You know I’ve experimented with other religions, but you know it’s like they say, you come right back to — a friend of mine in the World Saxophone Quartet, I’m not going to say who it is, but you know he was studying Indian religion, Ravi somebody, I can’t remember. And we were in a small earthquake in Berkeley one time and he ran out in his underwear screaming, “Save me Jesus.” So anyway, so I said, “Well what happened to the other religion thing?” He said, “Well I don’t know.” But the fact is, you know the way you’re brought up is pretty much the way you’re going to be, if it’s put into you the way it was put into me. And that’s my indoctrination. I could go and try to study different religions but when it comes down to it man, I’m going to go with what I know.
